summary: Migration expression/WHERE clause (A) and 23505 detection mechanism (B) are correct -- verified against node_modules/typeorm/error/QueryFailedError.js, which copies driverError's own enumerable properties (incl. code) onto the QueryFailedError instance itself, so err.code works. Mechanical mock fixes in dunning.service.spec.ts and guard-chain.integration.spec.ts (items 4/5) correctly match present-day production call sites, no masking. However the core race fix fails items C/D: handleSend's catch-and-refetch re-runs findByJobId() on the SAME queryRunner/transaction that just took the 23505 error when DATABASE_SESSION_CONTEXT_ENABLED=true (the actual staging config in .env.staging and staging.yml, and the documented production target per docs/runbooks/release-baseline-157-80.md). Postgres aborts a transaction after any statement error; the re-fetch query on the poisoned transaction throws Postgres error 25P02 ('current transaction is aborted'), which is uncaught and propagates out of runInTenantContext (which rolls back and rethrows) -- so handleSend throws instead of returning the winner's row, defeating the fix's purpose in exactly the environment where the race is real. The new regression test only exercises a hard-coded passthrough mock of runInTenantContext ((ctx, work) => work(undefined)), i.e. always the flag-OFF non-transactional path, so it is false-green for this failure mode. Ran the three named suites (notifications.processor.spec.ts, dunning.service.spec.ts, guard-chain.integration.spec.ts): 37/37 pass, confirming existing evidence does not cover this gap. Filed find-855bcd84 (HIGH).
